1: Chapter 1: A Visitor in the Rain
It had been raining on Pierrefeu for three days. In the spring, Claire Martin's elder sister had left for Paris, and since then Claire had run the village's little pharmacy alone.
After nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone knocked hard at the door downstairs. A man's voice called out: "Is anyone there?"
On the threshold stood a young man soaked to the bone, his left arm bound in a bloodstained cloth. He introduced himself: his name was Pierre Lapin, and he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"You have to treat me," Lapin said in a low voice. "I can pay. Three thousand five hundred francs — will that be enough?"
He took a letter wrapped in oiled paper from his jacket. "This letter must reach the abbey of Saint-Vent before the eighteenth of May."
Since her sister had left, Claire had often felt low in the evenings, but that night she had no time to think of it.
She refused his money all the same and said only: "Tomorrow at dawn I'll take you into the mountains."
2: At daybreak they set off. Claire carried a basket on her back holding bread, medicinal herbs and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope they met old Gaston Roux, who was splitting wood. He set down his axe and told them in a low voice that the evening before, three strangers had been questioning people at the entrance to the village about a wounded young man.
"Take the footpath, little Claire," said Gaston Roux. "The main road isn't safe." Claire thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Claire walked in front, setting each foot down with confidence. Lapin followed without a word.
At noon the rain stopped; the mist slowly cleared and the roof of the abbey of Saint-Vent appeared in the distance. At the door stood a nun, Sister Agnès, whose task it was to welcome visitors.
Sister Agnès took the letter, examined the red seal and nodded. "The Mother Abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Lapin said to Claire, "I owe you my life." Claire smiled. "Then next time, fix the roof of my pharmacy." Lapin stayed at the abbey.
In the evening Claire came down the mountain alone. When she reached home it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
